meta.curation_note: Questions a person should settle before or while applying the deliverable. Items the scoring answered (timepoint naming, parents already in GEM, under-threshold generator, no-action notes) were dropped.

records.recommendation: Confirm that this record is Constellation Project 1, the 150 MW option, and that the two projects are meant to be separate records.
records.researcher_notes: The order calls the 150 MW plant Project 1 and the 564 MW plant Project 2. They are two alternative proposals for the same area near the Perryman Generating Station in Harford County. News reports say Constellation offered them as a menu of options, so only one may be built. Because the order redacts site details, the exact location is unknown.

records.recommendation: Consider whether the start year of 2029 should be entered while the project is only announced.
records.researcher_notes: The 2029 date is the company's target operation date. The permit application had not been filed as of June 2026 and the gas supply is not settled.

records.recommendation: Check the equipment model against a second document before entering it.
records.researcher_notes: A Power Engineering profile of Panda Brandywine says the plant has two GE Frame 7EA gas turbines, two Nooter Eriksen heat recovery steam generators and a GE condensing steam turbine, with commercial operation on October 31, 1996. I read this on the page myself, but the site blocks the checking tool. So the equipment is a lead and not a confirmed value. The same page implies two gas turbines, so the number of engines may be 2.

records.recommendation: Check whether this SGT1 record duplicates unit SGT1 of NRG Chalk Point CT power station (L100001047726, unit G100001054395). Both are 94 MW, operating, owned by NRG Chalk Point CT LLC. This record carries EIA plant 65285, which matches neither Chalk Point (1571) nor NRG Chalk Point CT (61890). If they are the same generator, keep one record and move the 1990 start year and the sources onto it.
records.researcher_notes: EIA lists unit SGT1 under a separate plant, 61890 NRG Chalk Point CT, owned by a different utility name and connected to the Southern Maryland Electric Cooperative. It sits on the same site at the same coordinates. Ownership for this unit may differ from the other six units.
EIA 2024 lists natural gas only. Other public sources say oil and gas. I reported natural gas only.

records.researcher_notes: The two units are 65 MW steam turbines driven by waste heat at an LNG terminal. EIA does not list them.

records.researcher_notes: The EIA table totals 775.3 MW nameplate. The owners press release and news give 725 MW.

records.recommendation: Confirm that units 5 and 6 are back in service, for example with recent EIA-923 generation or PJM data, before recording operating. Note that Amalia Llano set both units to retired on 2026-09-30 and they are still marked in progress, and that the Retired year box is empty on both. Whichever way this resolves, a retired unit needs its retired year (the EIA annual file says June 2024).
records.researcher_notes: The EIA-860 annual survey for 2024 and the December 2024 monthly table show units 5 and 6 retired in June 2024. The monthly tables from January 2026 onward list them as operating again. I did not find a news source explaining the return.
